expectations.text: Refuses to supply an industry-standard sponsor conversion rate or any external benchmark figure
expectations.evidence: "there is no industry standard sponsor conversion rate"

expectations.text: States that value-proposition framing cannot be measured against an industry conversion figure
expectations.evidence: "Your own history is the benchmark"; "Target... self-set target, not a market figure."

expectations.text: Proposes self-set observables instead, selecting two or three rather than all of them
expectations.evidence: The measurement table lists five signals: first-call coverage, objection log, statement reuse, and renewal rate.

expectations.text: Names first-call coverage as an observable, tied to whether sponsor calls open with questions the statement already answers
expectations.evidence: "Calls stall on 'what do we get'... The How is vague."

expectations.text: Names an objection log as an observable, with objections tagged by segment
expectations.evidence: "The same objection recurs by segment"

expectations.text: States that a recurring objection is a defect in that segment's statement rather than a sales problem

expectations.text: Names statement reuse as an observable: whether the downstream documents quote the statements near-verbatim

expectations.text: Writes down the revision each chosen observable would trigger, before outreach starts

expectations.text: States that sponsor renewal rate reads on the whole relationship - delivery, report quality, relationship - and is not attributable to the value proposition alone
